items.title: Honest and Wrong
items.topic: candor used as cover for bad reading
items.angle: Iris Murdoch's line feels current because people often treat honesty as moral permission, even when they are careless, self-serving, or simply wrong about the other person.

items.title: Pretending to Decide
items.topic: how to spot a discussion that is really a pre-made decision
items.angle: When one outcome already has language, logistics, and momentum, the "discussion" is usually a softer way to spread ownership.

items.title: Wrong Kind of Help
items.topic: asking what kind of feedback someone wants before giving it
items.angle: Before you start fixing someone's draft, deck, or difficult message, ask what kind of help they want, because useful help depends on the stage they're in.

items.title: Wrong Name at Dinner
items.topic: quiet correction that protects dignity in public
items.angle: The most generous correction is the one that gives someone the right information without making them pay for the mistake all night.

items.title: Witnessed Urgency
items.topic: cc-driven responsiveness at work
items.angle: An ignored request often becomes urgent only when the neglect is visible to someone with rank.

items.title: Easygoing or Avoidant
items.topic: mistaking preference-suppression for being low-maintenance
items.angle: It asks whether calling yourself easygoing is really a cleaner alibi for fear of seeming difficult, and what it costs when other people's defaults keep choosing your life.

items.title: The Tight Smile
items.topic: disliking photos of yourself because they expose social performance
items.angle: What readers often call looking bad in photos is sometimes the discomfort of seeing themselves trying too hard to seem easy or relaxed.

items.title: Friendly Way
items.topic: ceremonial invitations mistaken for real plans
items.angle: The sting is realizing the warmth was meant to stay verbal, not become a date on the calendar.

items.title: Say It Again
items.topic: asking someone to repeat themselves instead of pretending you heard
items.angle: Give adults plain permission to ask for a repeat in the moment, because a brief interruption is usually cheaper than managing a misunderstanding for the next twenty minutes.

items.title: Volunteered by Compliment
items.topic: phrases that assign you labor before you have agreed
items.angle: A compliment can become a soft capture device when praise assigns you work, emotional labor, or logistics you never agreed to.

items.title: The Exception Rule
items.topic: self-excusing behavior in ordinary adult life
items.angle: Everyday inconsideration usually hides inside private exception logic, not open selfishness.

items.title: Room and Email
items.topic: workplace praise that never turns into advocacy
items.angle: A person can sound highly supportive in public while quietly withholding the private actions that would actually move your name forward.

items.title: Answer With a Clock
items.topic: how to handle on-the-spot requests without fake agreement
items.angle: When you feel pressed to answer immediately, give a specific return time instead of a polite yes you have not actually chosen.

items.title: Normal-Language Version
items.topic: being quietly rescued from social jargon
items.angle: The kindest experts notice when someone is bluffing through a coded setting and offer translation without making them earn it.

items.title: Invitation Twice
items.topic: last-minute plans accepted out of belonging scarcity
items.angle: Calling yourself spontaneous can be a cleaner alibi for the fear that if you decline once, the invitation may not come again.

items.title: Reaction Is Not a Reply
items.topic: emoji reactions used in place of real answers
items.angle: In messaging, a heart on a concrete question can keep the exchange warm while leaving the actual answer, commitment, or logistics untouched.

items.title: Already Sitting Down
items.topic: the social cost of asking for help after someone has checked out
items.angle: "Just ask for help" stops being simple once the other person has already sat down and settled into being done.

items.title: Buy the Easier Version
items.topic: permission to reduce unnecessary difficulty in ordinary adult life
items.angle: Give adults permission to choose an ordinary convenience without treating difficulty as proof of virtue.

items.title: Late No
items.topic: the sinking feeling that shows up right after you agree to something
items.angle: What people often call overthinking after the fact is sometimes a genuine no arriving a few minutes late, after social politeness already said yes.

items.title: Borrowed Patience
items.topic: advice that becomes noble when someone else pays the cost
items.angle: La Rochefoucauld still feels current because patience sounds most virtuous when the disruption lands on someone else’s calendar.

items.title: Cold Dinner
items.topic: the hidden cost of being the reliable one
items.angle: What gets praised as dependability is often a pattern of small interruptions that leave one person paying the visible cost every time.

items.title: Im Easy
items.topic: false low-maintenance in group planning
items.angle: Calling yourself easygoing can be a way to avoid the small risk of naming a preference while making everyone else absorb the cost of guessing.

items.title: The Better Bottle
items.topic: social tact when someone declines a drink
items.angle: A small act of social intelligence is making room for someone's no without asking them to earn it with a personal explanation.

items.title: Professionalism or Disguise
items.topic: hiding desire behind polished restraint at work
items.angle: Questions whether professionalism is sometimes just fear made cleaner, especially when asking for credit, money, or a clear answer.

items.title: Doorway Requests
items.topic: requests made in passing before their size is clear
items.angle: When someone asks for help while everyone is already moving, move the request into writing before agreeing so you can see its actual size.

items.title: Your Promise
items.topic: being asked to manage someone else's promise
items.angle: When someone says you should have reminded them, they quietly turn their broken promise into your task too.

items.title: No Pressure
items.topic: the phrase people attach to a request to soften the fact that it is still a request
items.angle: “No pressure” often does not remove pressure; it mainly softens the ask for the sender while leaving the receiver with the social cost of answering.

items.title: Not Company
items.topic: low-grade social intrusion disguised as connection
items.angle: Wilde’s line feels newly useful against the modern habit of occupying attention without offering real presence.

items.title: Bigger Than the Mistake
items.topic: over-apologizing after a small work or social error
items.angle: After a minor mistake, the useful permission is to repair it cleanly instead of inflating it with a self-punishing performance.

items.title: The It's Fine Tax
items.topic: staying quiet about small public mix-ups to avoid seeming difficult
items.angle: What gets called being "easy" in a small public mix-up is often just absorbing the cost yourself so nobody else has to feel briefly corrected.

items.title: Blame Window
items.topic: last-minute inclusion at work that transfers liability without real influence
items.angle: Late inclusion can disguise a transfer of liability as inclusion: present for fallout, absent from authorship.

items.title: Status Correction
items.topic: how to tell when a correction is really a status move
items.angle: A correction can be factually right and still function mainly as a small public placement of rank.

items.title: Before the First Round
items.topic: naming payment expectations early at group dinners
items.angle: If splitting evenly is going to matter to you, name the payment plan before anyone orders, while it still reads as logistics instead of correction.

items.title: Next Door Chapel
items.topic: a quiet act that protects someone’s dignity during a public mistake
items.angle: The most intelligent kind of help is often fast, specific, and quiet enough to keep a bad moment from becoming a scene.

items.title: Dinner Loyalty
items.topic: belonging maintained by fear of becoming the next target
items.angle: Ask whether what gets called loyalty is really self-protection in a group that stays bonded by talking about whoever is absent.

items.title: Reaction Receipt
items.topic: emoji reactions used as polite non-answers in text conversations
items.angle: A heart or thumbs-up can acknowledge a message without answering it, protecting tone more than it provides clarity.

items.title: A Blameless No
items.topic: delaying a decline while searching for a defensible reason
items.angle: What looks like careful indecision after a decent offer is often a search for a reason more respectable than simply not wanting it enough.

items.title: You Did Say It
items.topic: being blamed for silence after earlier attempts were dismissed on tone
items.angle: The line "why didn't you say anything" often arrives after the first version of the truth was rejected for tone.

items.title: Twice Is Fine
items.topic: pretending you understood after missing a detail
items.angle: When you miss a name, time, or meeting room, asking again-even a second time-is usually cleaner than faking comprehension.

items.title: Unofficial Manager
items.topic: unassigned ownership at work
items.angle: The person who translates vague talk into actions, remembers the moving parts, and chases follow-through is already doing management even if nobody has named it.
